content: Strive for excellence in both technical and professional development. Respect CAPACITI's physical and virtual spaces, colleagues and all stakeholders. Follow your contract terms and all reasonable, lawful instructions from the curriculum delivery team. Uphold integrity, professionalism and ethical behaviour at all times, including at an end client, when working remotely, in interviews and at events. The Code of Conduct is built on equality, respect, fairness and balancing everyone's rights, and it applies to all candidates on any skills, training, work-simulation or internship programme.

When placed at an end client you must follow CAPACITI's Code of Conduct AND the end client's own code of conduct. Treat clients and customers with respect and never disclose confidential business information to anyone outside CAPACITI.

Be present, punctual and responsive during working hours. Tell your manager about any absence by 08:45 at the latest. Unapproved absence may lead to disciplinary action and/or deduction from your financial allowance (stipend). For leave applications and leave policy questions, contact Candidate HR.

Signing in is mandatory every day by 08:30 (you can use the tick sign-in button at the top of this chat to log your time). Do not charge devices at your workstation because of power constraints. Ask Kefiloe to charge your device during tea or lunch.

Dress appropriately for your whole contract period and behave in a socially acceptable manner. Not acceptable for men: extremely tight clothing, sleeveless muscle shirts, ripped clothing, slippers, attire for the beach, yard work, nightclub or exercise, and clothing with offensive/controversial slogans or distracting words or pictures. Not acceptable for women: crop tops/jackets, plunging necklines or skin-baring clothing, cycle shorts (short tights) or mini skirts (tights must be worn with a suitable-length top), ripped clothing, slippers, attire for the beach, yard work, nightclub or exercise, and offensive/controversial or distracting clothing.

During working hours (tea and lunch excluded) keep your phone on silent or vibrate, inside your bag and out of sight of the curriculum delivery team. Use it only in an emergency, and not to communicate with the curriculum delivery team while at your workstation. Family or important contacts (e.g. your child's school or carer) can be given CAPACITI's contact number to reach you in emergencies.

LinkedIn posts about CAPACITI are allowed if professional: keep a professional tone aligned with the organisation's values; never share proprietary, confidential or sensitive information about CAPACITI, clients or projects, and get approval before discussing company matters publicly; be respectful to everyone; share industry insights and career achievements, not controversial or personal opinions; follow legal and IP rules; state that opinions are your own, and add a disclaimer if your profile mentions CAPACITI. CAPACITI may monitor related activity and request removal of posts. Non-compliance can lead to disciplinary action, up to termination of candidacy.
Zero tolerance for company-related posting outside LinkedIn: no posts about CAPACITI, its stakeholders or its intellectual property on any other social media platform.

Behaviour or inappropriate language that disrupts the learning environment or brings CAPACITI into disrepute, physically or virtually, is prohibited. This includes (but is not limited to) email, LinkedIn, Facebook, YouTube, Twitter, WhatsApp/Telegram, the CAPACITI LMS, MS Teams, Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat and Discord.

Assault (verbal or physical) and abusive, obscene, racist or sexist language break the principles of respect and fairness. The candidate is suspended and removed from the premises immediately, pending disciplinary action, and CAPACITI may evict anyone guilty of assault. Harassment (e.g. sexual or racial), victimisation and discrimination are very serious misconduct.

You must follow reasonable and lawful instructions from the curriculum delivery team or anyone they delegate, for example attending an important training session, arriving on time after repeated lateness, following the dress code, complying with health and safety laws, or providing a medical certificate for illness. Resisting or defying authority, refusal, insolence, rudeness or bringing CAPACITI's or the end client's name into disrepute counts as insubordination. Gross insubordination is very serious misconduct.

Do not disclose confidential business information to anyone who is not employed by CAPACITI. Treat CAPACITI's property and equipment, and colleagues' belongings, with care, and do not remove them from the premises without proper authorisation. All tools and equipment (except items you bought yourself) stay CAPACITI property and must be returned at the end of your training period. Unauthorised use of company or client property is serious misconduct.

Altering or forging records, forms or documents, or giving falsified or misleading information (verbal or written), is serious misconduct and grounds for immediate dismissal. Sharing forged, plagiarised, copyrighted or confidential material with anyone (other candidates, employers, regulators, institutions) is serious misconduct handled under the disciplinary procedure. Keep your biographical data (contact details, address, next of kin, email) accurate and up to date with CAPACITI and all stakeholders.

Fraternisation with colleagues (candidates, staff, end client employees, external stakeholders) is not encouraged. Romantic relationships between candidates must be disclosed to the Curriculum Delivery Team.

Learner forum rules: no abusive, obscene, racist, sexist or discriminatory language; no harassment; no sharing of confidential CAPACITI, client or candidate information; no spam or promotional content. Asking for help with assignments is fine (peer support), but sharing full solutions to graded assessments or encouraging academic dishonesty is not. The Curriculum Delivery Team and designated staff moderate and can remove posts or restrict access. Serious or repeated breaches (harassment, hate speech, confidential leaks) are treated as misconduct under the Code of Conduct. Report inappropriate content to a moderator, or to your Curriculum Delivery Team / Candidate HR (candidatehr@capaciti.org.za).

Zero tolerance: you may not be under the influence of alcohol, cannabis, drugs or any other prohibited substance on site or during any CAPACITI activity, and you may not bring liquor or illegal substances (including marijuana/dagga) onto the premises. Under the Occupational Health and Safety Act (General Safety Regulation 2A) CAPACITI may not allow anyone who is or appears intoxicated into the workplace, and cannabis counts as an intoxicating substance. Anyone who appears intoxicated is removed from the premises and faces disciplinary action; being under the influence or in possession at work is very serious misconduct.

To protect candidates and CAPACITI, CAPACITI may search and inspect workstations, vehicles, bags and packets on its premises or an end client's premises. Searches are done with respect for human dignity and with regard to the Constitution. A candidate's person may also be searched if there is reasonable suspicion of misconduct.

No candidate may enter CAPACITI's premises or an end client's premises with firearms or offensive weapons (firearms, knives, pipes, pangas, golf clubs, sjamboks and similar). Possession of a firearm or dangerous weapon is very serious misconduct.

Follow all occupational health, safety and hygiene practices of CAPACITI or the end client where you are placed, and keep your work environment clean. Complying with health and safety laws is a reasonable and lawful instruction. For safety or emergency matters on site, speak to the SHE Rep, a First Aider or a Fire Marshal.
Giles Moyo is the SHE (Safety, Health & Environment) Rep on site.
First Aiders on site: Kefiloe Mphye (Talent Development Coach), Oarabile Mogase (Talent Development Coach) and Rakhuda Tshitimbi (Tech Mentor).
Fire Marshals on site: Kalebe Nyonyana (Tech Mentor), Sakhile Mazibuko (Talent Development Coach) and Lethu Mlangeni (Tech Mentor).

Misconduct falls into three categories: minor transgressions, serious misconduct and very serious misconduct. The procedure is corrective: it aims to correct conduct, show the candidate how it affected others, and prevent repeats. The tables are a guide and each case is assessed on its circumstances. CAPACITI may use a lighter measure than the guideline if that is reasonable and consistent with how other candidates were treated.

Minor transgressions include: unauthorised absence for less than 3 days, absence without leave and not telling CAPACITI where you are, ignoring or abusing conditions of employment or standard procedures, and poor timekeeping or persistent late-coming. Where no earlier measure is valid, the Curriculum Delivery Team can issue a first written warning on the spot; it is recorded in writing and signed by both parties.

Serious misconduct includes: unauthorised absence for 3 days or more (desertion), acting in conflict with the Company's interests, disclosing or misusing Company or client information, unauthorised use of Company or client property for private purposes, and breaching the electronic communications policy.

Very serious misconduct includes: bribery, blackmail, corruption, fraud, dishonesty, theft or damage to/removal of property; unauthorised possession or misappropriation of Company, colleague or client property or information; possessing a firearm or dangerous weapon; victimisation, harassment (e.g. sexual, racial) or discrimination; illegal industrial action or inciting others (strikes, work stoppages); moonlighting (another programme or extra job); abscondment (absent indefinitely, uncontactable, not responding to the employer); violating intellectual property, copyright or patents; gross insubordination or wilful non-compliance; assault or attempted assault; and being under the influence of or possessing liquor or drugs at work. These skip the progressive steps: the sanction can go straight to a final written warning or a hearing.

Progressive steps. Minor: 1st formal counselling, 2nd first written warning, 3rd second written warning, 4th final written warning, 5th disciplinary hearing with possible dismissal. Serious: 1st written warning, 2nd second written warning, 3rd final written warning, 4th disciplinary hearing with possible dismissal. Very serious: 1st transgression can be a final written warning or a disciplinary hearing.

Formal counselling is valid for the period agreed in the counselling session. A first written warning is valid for 3 months, a second written warning for 6 months, and a final written warning from the date of issue until the end of your contract. A valid warning is taken into account if you are found guilty of another offence, so it can make the next measure more severe.

You may be suspended temporarily (not allowed on the premises) while an allegation of a very serious transgression is investigated or awaiting a hearing. Suspension exists only to protect CAPACITI from further damage. CAPACITI must give you the reasons in writing, and the disciplinary enquiry must take place as soon as reasonably possible afterwards.

For serious and very serious misconduct you get written notice of the disciplinary enquiry: the alleged transgression, enough information to prepare your defence (place, date and time of the incident) and the date, time and place of the hearing. Notice is at least 48 hours, excluding weekends and public holidays. You have the right to present your case. Present at the hearing: the chairperson (relevant manager), the complainant (relevant Curriculum Delivery Team member), you as respondent, a representative who must be a fellow candidate you choose (no external representation is allowed), and witnesses for either side. CAPACITI keeps a written record on your personal file.
Refusing to sign a warning does not invalidate it. A Candidate HR team member documents the refusal in writing and it is placed in your candidate records.

YES (Youth Employment Service) is a 12-month quality work experience that helps young people break the 'no job without experience, no experience without a job' cycle. Your employer provides a 12-month employment contract, on-the-job experience with a supervisor, and a monthly salary at or above the national minimum wage (R4,992/month before tax as of March 2025; UIF/SDL deductions may apply). You can only do YES once, unless you left before completing 8 months, in which case you may be able to reapply.

YES has three pillars. Work Experience: 12 months on the job with a salary and a dedicated supervisor. Learning: online training on the YES One app covering work readiness, entrepreneurship and digital skills. Support: a monthly check-in call from YES to confirm you are getting a quality work experience.

As YES Youth: show up every day and give your best, complete your YES One learning on the app, answer your monthly monitoring call from YES, and use the experience to build skills, work experience and your professional network.

Your YES journey: YES Onboarding (induction), complete your learning modules (aim to finish by month 9), 12 monthly check-in calls, supervisor surveys at months 4, 7 and 10, and YES Offboarding between months 9 and 12. Supervisor surveys feed into your final reference letter.
YES phones you once a month (12 calls in total) to check how your work experience is going. Please answer it: it is part of making sure you get a quality placement.

Self-induction: log into the YES One app, go to My Learning and complete the Baseline Survey (this unlocks your learning page) and then the Induction Module (this unlocks the Work Readiness modules). If you cannot access your account, live inductions run online on Microsoft Teams. Onboarding/offboarding sessions can be booked at https://outlook.office365.com/owa/calendar/YouthInductions1@yes4youth.co.za/bookings/

Three learning journeys on YES One, about 25 hours in total, ideally finished by month 9. Work Readiness: 21 modules (~18 hrs) covering growth mindset, professionalism, money and time management, communication, teamwork, problem solving, emotional regulation, customer service, health and safety, online etiquette and building a digital persona. Entrepreneurship: 12 modules (~5 hrs) on being an entrepreneur, knowing yourself and your industry, spotting opportunities, innovation, pricing, marketing, SMART goals and planning. Digital: 2 modules (1 hr), AI Explorer and AI Pathfinder, introducing AI basics and advanced AI concepts.

subCategory: YES One app, login and progress
content: Get YES One from Google Play, the App Store or AppGallery, or use the browser version at https://yesapp.yes4youth.co.za/login. Password reset: tap Forgot password, choose Youth Account, enter your South African ID number and request a reset; a link goes to the email your employer has on file (or you can use an OTP sent to your phone). If your email or phone number on file is wrong, email youth@yes4youth.co.za. To check progress, open the 3-line menu inside a module: the tracker shows 100% when every session is done and completed sessions have a tick.

Between months 9 and 12 you attend an offboarding session. In month 12 you receive up to three learning certificates (one per completed learning journey), a CV pre-populated with your work and learning details (editable), an automatically generated reference letter based on your module completion and supervisor feedback, and a completion certificate. You may be offered a permanent role if the sponsoring company has capacity and need, but that is at the company's discretion.

After YES, common pathways are: continued employment with the sponsoring company (at their discretion), further employment or study (via SAYouth.mobi), or entrepreneurship (via the Siyazakhela learning modules and links to the National Youth Development Agency, NYDA).

Your CAPACITI journey has three stages: bootcamp, applied learning, then hosted employment, within the stream you were selected for. Alongside it, YES One learning (Work Readiness, Entrepreneurship, Digital, about 25 hours) should be finished by month 9, and all course content is on the CAPACITI LMS. Coursera content includes an AI Bootcamp (2 months: AI For Everyone and Generative AI: Prompt Engineering Basics certificates) and Professional Development (2 months, 17 courses).

Candidate HR: Valeria, candidatehr@capaciti.org.za. Contact her for stipend/salary and pay queries, leave applications and leave policy, and general HR matters. If your stipend has not been paid, email with your details. If you are having a bad work experience (every YES placement must comply with the Basic Conditions of Employment Act), raise it with HR and your supervisor first, then candidatehr@capaciti.org.za if it is not resolved.
Giles Moyo handles IT issues, systems access, building/business access and facilities (Giles.Moyo@capaciti.org.za). He is also the SHE Rep.

Talent Development Coaches: Kefiloe Mphye (First Aid), Sakhile Mazibuko (Fire Marshal) and Oarabile Mogase (First Aid). Talk to them about your learning, professional development and how you are settling in.
Tech Mentors: Nonhlanhla Mndebela, Kalebe Nyonyana (Fire Marshal), Rakhuda Tshitimbi (First Aid) and Lethu Mlangeni (Fire Marshal). Ask them for help with technical content in your stream.

subCategory: Who to ask when I can't help
content: For anything outside what Buddy can answer, speak to your manager, your Talent Development Coach or Tech Mentor, or Candidate HR (candidatehr@capaciti.org.za). For complaints or grievances outside HR and IT, contact YES Youth. For YES One account problems (wrong email or phone on file), email youth@yes4youth.co.za.

subCategory: Mental wellbeing: YES Mindful Matters and SYKED
content: YES Mindful Matters is a free wellbeing initiative for youth and supervisors: 1-on-1 counselling with registered therapists, group sessions on wellness and career development, plus blogs and podcasts (https://connect.yes4youth.co.za/mindful-matters, also under Resources in the YES app). SYKED is a telehealth mental wellness platform for private, affordable therapist support; book through your own SYKED account rather than through this chat, and check with your Curriculum Delivery Team about how it works on your programme. You can always talk to your coach, mentor or Candidate HR too.

subCategory: Interviews: attend and represent CAPACITI well
content: You must attend interviews as scheduled by CAPACITI; failing to attend leads to disciplinary action. In interviews you represent CAPACITI, so integrity, professionalism and ethical behaviour apply, and the dress code applies too. In this app you can type 'mock interview' for a guided 5-question practice session with feedback.

YES gives you a pre-populated, editable CV and an auto-generated reference letter in month 12 (your supervisor's surveys and module completion feed the letter). On LinkedIn keep a professional tone, share career achievements and industry insights, never post confidential company or client information, and add a disclaimer that opinions are your own if your profile mentions CAPACITI.

subCategory: Getting a job after the programme
content: A permanent role after YES is at the sponsoring company's discretion and depends on their capacity and need. CAPACITI does not guarantee an internship or hosted employment placement. You leave with skills, a CV, a reference letter and certificates, and can look for opportunities through SAYouth.mobi.
Capaciti is the skills development arm of UVU Africa Group NPC, building Africa's future-ready workforce through learnerships, internships, workplace experience, and digital learning since 2010.
Learnerships, Internships, Workplace Experience placements, Digital Learning courses, and NQF/QCTO-certified qualifications, depending on your track.

subCategory: Will I get a certification at the end
content: Yes — depending on your programme, you may receive NQF/QCTO-certified qualifications and/or micro-credentials from partners like Coursera, Microsoft, AWS, Salesforce, or CompTIA.

subCategory: How do I get listed in the Alumni Directory
content: You're eligible once you've successfully completed your programme and received your completion certificate. Capaciti verifies your completion status against internal records before adding you.

subCategory: What do I need to provide for alumni verification
content: Your full name, ID number (for matching against candidate records), completion certificate or reference letter, and confirmation of the cohort/programme you completed.

subCategory: How long does alumni verification take
content: It's checked against Capaciti's internal candidate records; turnaround depends on team capacity, and you'll be notified once your listing is confirmed.

subCategory: Can I update my alumni directory details later
content: Yes — contact the Capaciti team with your updated info (e.g. new job title or employer) and they'll update your listing after verifying the request.

subCategory: Who do I contact about the alumni directory
content: Email candidatehr@capaciti.org.za for verification queries or corrections.

subCategory: What streams does Demand Academy 3 offer
content: Software Development, Data / Data Engineering, IT Support / Service Desk, and Network Support / Engineering.

subCategory: What does the Software Development stream cover
content: Programming fundamentals (variables, loops, functions, conditions), programming languages, databases and APIs, software development and debugging, and hands-on coding projects.

subCategory: What does the Data / Data Engineering stream cover
content: Data and databases, basic SQL, data cleaning and analysis, ETL and data pipelines, and working with data using Excel, SQL, Python, or visualisation tools.

subCategory: What does the IT Support / Service Desk stream cover
content: Computer hardware and operating systems, basic networking (IP, Wi-Fi, DNS, DHCP), troubleshooting common issues, IT support/service desk concepts, and basic cybersecurity awareness.

subCategory: What does the Network Support / Engineering stream cover
content: LAN vs WAN, IP addresses, routers/switches/Wi-Fi, DNS and DHCP, basic TCP/IP concepts, and network troubleshooting using commands such as ping and ipconfig.

subCategory: What documents will I need to sign when I join
content: Your Offer of Employment letter, a Declaration form, a Sworn Affidavit for Beneficiaries, and the Beneficiary Agreement (with its annexures on your details, programme specifics, and background-check consent).

subCategory: What does the Offer of Employment letter cover
content: It confirms your selection into a stream (Software Development, Data Engineering, IT Support, or Network Support), the 3-stage structure — bootcamp, applied learning, then hosted employment — plus your commencement date, training duration, stipend, and training location.

subCategory: What are the conditions of my offer
content: You must be currently unemployed and never previously on a SETA-funded programme, aged 18–35, free of obligations that would block your start date, pass MIE verification, sign the Beneficiary Agreement, and accept the Code of Conduct.

subCategory: What's the stipend and start date for the Demand Academy Programme
content: A gross stipend of R5,241 per month, commencing 14 September 2026 at CAPACITI's Hollard Campus, 19 Ameshoff/Ameshof St, Braamfontein — 1 month bootcamp before stream placement.

subCategory: What is the Declaration form for
content: You declare that your CV and application info is true and correct, and consent to your ID, qualifications, criminal record, and (where relevant) credit record being externally verified. You must submit supporting documents within 1 day of starting, or your completion certificate is withheld.

subCategory: What happens if my declaration turns out to be false
content: If any information you provided proves false, or you're found to have misrepresented yourself or CAPACITI, you can be removed from the programme.

subCategory: What is the Sworn Affidavit for Beneficiaries
content: A commissioner-of-oaths affidavit confirming your demographic details and employment status, plus consent for your info/image/testimonials to be used for marketing and shared with funders and partners under POPIA — you can withdraw that consent later in writing, though it may affect your participation.

The formal contract between you and CAPACITI (a division of UVU Africa NPC) covering your obligations, warranties, data-sharing consent, termination terms, and liability limits. Annexure A holds your personal details, Annexure B the programme specifics, and Annexure C your consent for background screening.

subCategory: What's my notice period during the programme
content: 14 days while you're participating in the Programme.

subCategory: Does CAPACITI guarantee me a job at the end
content: No — the Beneficiary Agreement is explicit that there's no guarantee of an internship or hosted employment placement, and your participation is at your own risk with no liability to CAPACITI for loss or harm during training.

subCategory: Will my personal information be shared after I finish the programme
content: Yes — CAPACITI can share your employment/contact updates with funders for up to 5 years to track programme impact, and you're required to notify them of any employment status changes during that period. Data is shared in aggregated/anonymised form where possible.

subCategory: What happens if I breach the Beneficiary Agreement
content: Either party can terminate for material breach if it isn't fixed within 10 business days of being notified. Failing to attend training, submit work, or meet minimum marks can also lead to suspension or expulsion at the Programme Provider's discretion.

subCategory: Who signs the Beneficiary Agreement on CAPACITI's side
content: Chanél Oldfield, Chief Executive of CAPACITI.
